answer: A subject I would love to study in the future is psychology, which I find [[endlessly fascinating]]. I have always been curious about why people think and behave the way they do. I became interested in it after reading a few popular books on the topic, which completely [[captivated]] me. My job has made that interest even stronger, because I meet many students who are anxious about their future, and I often wish I understood their worries better. I would ideally study it formally, perhaps through a postgraduate course, as I feel it deserves proper, in-depth study. Since my background is in business administration, I might first take a short introductory course online to see whether I can cope with the scientific side of it. What appeals to me most is how [[applicable]] it is to everyday life; understanding human behaviour is useful in almost any profession. I think it would help me become more [[empathetic]] and a better communicator, both personally and professionally. In my line of work, being able to read people and put them at ease is half the job. Honestly, I believe it is one of those subjects that genuinely changes how you see the world. You start noticing patterns in your own behaviour, and you become a little more patient with others. It bridges science and human experience in a way I find deeply appealing. It is definitely something I hope to pursue once my circumstances allow, because I think it would enrich both my career and my understanding of the people around me.

followUps.q: Would you like to work as a psychologist?
followUps.answer: Probably not as a full-time psychologist. I'd rather use what I learn in education and counselling, helping students manage stress and make confident decisions about their studies and careers.

followUps.q: Is psychology a popular subject in your country?
followUps.answer: It is becoming more popular, especially in Dhaka. A generation ago, people rarely talked about mental health, but young people now are much more open, so interest in the subject has grown [[considerably]].

note: Linked interest to counselling anxious students at work, added a realistic first step given his BBA; mark 'fascinating' widened to [[endlessly fascinating]].
